messages:
Sam W: FYI support just escalated a billing-double report after a customer upgraded to sdk-js v3.1.0. They call POST /v1/charges and saw 502 -> client retried -> duplicate charge. logs attached (snippet).
Sam W: ```
[2026-03-10T14:12:05Z] POST /v1/charges 502
[2026-03-10T14:12:05Z] retrying request (attempt=2)
[2026-03-10T14:12:06Z] POST /v1/charges 200  # matched charge created again
``` 
Anya P: oh no. do we know if the client was sending the idempotency header? ask customer for their X-Idempotency-Key header value if present.
Sam W: customer says they upgraded from sdk-js 2.8.4 -> 3.1.0 and did NOT see X-Idempotency-Key in outgoing request in their capture. they assert v2 was sending it fine.
Mike R: I can repro locally. brief notes: regen'd client for JS template used the new OpenAPI spec where header param name changed from "X-Idempotency-Key" to "Idempotency-Key" (spec-level rename). our codegen generator maps header.name -> headerName in generated code but the template expects 'x-name' or lowercased headerKey; the mapping missed casing so header emit got dropped.
Mike R: repro steps (JS):
```bash
# checkout sdk-js@local-regen
npm i
node test/repro/charge-retry.js
# charge-retry.js: single POST without manual idempotency header, then trigger 502 from proxy and see retry
``` 
Mike R: both python and go generators produced the same omission for 3.1.0 because they share the openapi->param mapping util. so cross-SDK regression.
Anya P: how did CI miss this? sounds like spec changed but changelog entry missing.
Mike R: CI regen job (regenerate-clients) runs but our integration smoke doesn't assert presence of idempotency header for create endpoints. the OpenAPI change had no breaking-change flag and no human-review tag, so it slipped through. changelog gap = root cause for ops teams not being alerted.
Sam W: support asks for quick mitigation (customer already refunded but wants root cause + patch).
Leo D: propose hotfix: generator fallback that preserves header when param.name case-insensitively matches /idempotency(-|_)key/. quick patch in templates to emit header mapping if either 'name' or 'x-name' present. then cut sdk-js 3.1.1, sdk-py 3.1.1, sdk-go 3.1.1.
Anya P: +1. also add a regen CI guard: after generation, run a small linter that scans generated clients for presence of header constant (IDEMPOTENCY_HEADER) or binding for operations with x-idempotency usage. fail CI if missing.
Mike R: I can open the PR for generator template patch and add a tst in regen-integration that regenerates a tiny spec and asserts header preserved. will include a quick rollback script for customers to pin to sdk v2 if needed.
regen-bot: CI job 'regen-clients' triggered: job/regen-clients#458 failed on sdk-js lint (expected header constant missing) — see https://ci.redwood/regen/458
Leo D: I'll cut the emergency patch release once PR is green. also updating support playbook entry: "if customer reports duplicated charge after regen, check client version and X-Idempotency-Key presence in captures".
Sam W: thx all. I'll update the support ticket with repro steps and link to PR when opened. :thumbsup:
Anya P: for postmortem, we should require a changelog note on any OpenAPI header/name changes and add a cross-sdk regen-canary that runs against real sample requests. small followup item.
Mike R: noted. I added two TODOs to the regen backlog: (1) header-name-casing fallback in generator, (2) regen-canary test + changelog gating. will attach PR numbers.
Leo D: reaction :white_check_mark:
Sam W: closing loop with support in ~1h once patch release is published.
